<reason>CON built and sustained one clean line — a universal, always-on notice informs nobody because signals only work when they discriminate, and every benefit PRO claimed (audits, bias complaints) requires the criteria disclosure PRO explicitly disavowed in [A1.6]. PRO's "self-refutation" charge was neutralized by CON's three-prong fork ([B2.1]), PRO's nutrition-facts analogy was turned against it ([B2.3]), and PRO's credit-notice pressure question was answered with a persuasive distinction (specific decision, reasons given, lever attached). PRO's best move — forcing CON to name acceptable disclosures — did land, and the "floor not ceiling" reframe was reasonable, but CON's answer was coherent and CON's closing sharply showed that PRO's own stakes line ("no user hears matching as scoring desirability") describes information the mandated sentence wouldn't convey. PRO's concrete complaint ("curated pool presented as organic") was weak and effectively dismantled. Both sides were epistemically disciplined; CON had two clipped turns to PRO's one, a minor execution cost, but the argumentative edge was clearly CON's.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B2.1]–[B2.4] response to PRO's "self-refutation" charge: separating the sentence (obvious), the right (litigated), and the useful version (criteria that arm exploiters), then showing PRO's nutrition-label analogy actually describes the substantive disclosure PRO refused to defend. This fork framed the rest of the debate and PRO never escaped it.</best_rebuttal>
